hints: Look at the other symbols in $I = Anvq$: $A$ is cross-sectional area and $v$ is mean drift velocity, so $Av$ is volume swept per second.
Only electrons free to move through the metal lattice contribute to drift current, not electrons bound in atoms.
Check the wording difference between per unit volume and per atom, and between free electrons and total electrons.
walkthrough: Identify the expression $I = Anvq$ for a metal wire, where $A$ is cross-sectional area, $v$ is mean drift velocity of carriers and $q$ is charge of each carrier.
Recall the model: in time $t$ carriers move distance $vt$, so the volume passing a section is $Avt$ and the number of carriers passing is $nAvt$.
Multiply by $q$ to get charge passed: $Q = nAvtq$, then $I = Q/t = nAvq$, so $n$ must make $nAvt$ a number of carriers.
Therefore $n$ must be number of mobile carriers per unit volume, with unit $\text{m}^{-3}$, which for a metal means free conduction electrons.
This excludes atoms per unit volume, electrons per atom, and bound electrons that cannot drift. This is option C.

options.A: Atoms per unit volume counts lattice ions, not the mobile charge carriers that form $I$ in $I = Anvq$.
options.B: Free electrons per atom is a pure number per atom, not a number per unit volume as required for $n$.
options.C: In $I = Anvq$, $n$ is the number density of charge carriers that can drift, so free electrons per unit volume.
options.D: Total electrons per unit volume includes bound electrons that do not drift and do not contribute to $I$.
